**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hide task links until event operations are enabled**

This renders the task CTA for every valid logistics activity even though the adapter migrations are deliberately absent from the production manifest and `event.operations.api` defaults to disabled. In that deployment state, clicking the newly exposed button always reaches `requireEventOperationsEnabled`, receives a 404 `feature_disabled`, and leaves the user on the generic task error screen. Gate the link on actual feature availability or defer exposing it until activation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5c9bb3b5daf82fa438fe9f0dd1b796afd699d0a6. Removed the logistics task CTA while the adapter migrations remain outside the production manifest and event.operations.api defaults disabled. Direct routes and isolated enabled adapter tests remain intact. The activation contract and gap matrix now explicitly defer discoverable links until an authenticated backend availability contract and separately reviewed activation. No flag, migration or security control was enabled.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh follow state after a late successful mutation**

When a follow/unfollow request succeeds after the user changes profile or otherwise changes the location key, `isCurrent()` is false and this early return skips every cache invalidation. The server mutation has still committed, but the shared `['fan-follows', viewerId]` query remains stale across the newly rendered profile and even after returning to the original one, so the UI can offer the opposite action until an unrelated refetch occurs. Keep the navigation-specific analytics/resume effects fenced, but invalidate the shared follow data after every successful mutation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5c9bb3b5daf82fa438fe9f0dd1b796afd699d0a6. Successful follow and unfollow writes now invalidate the original viewer, artist directory and profile cache before the current-navigation guard. Analytics and resume navigation remain fenced. Two delayed-mutation component regressions verify shared data refreshes on the newly rendered profile and the correct action after returning; all five previous logout/session/unmount/navigation suppression cases remain intact. The focused UI run passes 27 tests.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hold the feature flag lock through lifecycle commands**

When an operator disables `event.operations.api` after this unlocked check has passed, the flag update can commit while the transition continues, allowing state, audit, and receipt writes to commit after the kill switch is disabled. Both checks use plain `EXISTS`, so even the later recheck only narrows the race; acquire a shared row lock on the enabled flag and retain it through the transaction, as the snapshot and task command functions do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in `34ca75d3d92d2a6def22e63ddd47baa96edca878`. The lifecycle function now takes a shared lock on the enabled feature-flag row before the event row and retains it through transaction completion, matching task/snapshot lock order. The native PostgreSQL16 regression reproduces the old command-first race, then verifies both command-first and disable-first orders at READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE using observed blocking relationships. All existing migration/replay/rollback assertions also pass. This adapter remains outside the 160-entry production manifest, whose SQL files are unchanged. Current-head hosted CI and fresh independent approval remain required.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate transition receipts before committing**

If the SQL function returns a malformed or target-mismatched receipt after staging a transition—such as during a function/schema regression—`runEventOperationsSessionDb` commits before the decoding at lines 186–197 runs. The handler then returns `invalid_database_response`, but the lifecycle change, audit, and receipt are already durable, unlike the newer RACI/completion boundaries that deliberately validate inside `SqlPersistT`; move strict receipt decoding and target/key/version binding into this transaction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in `34ca75d3d92d2a6def22e63ddd47baa96edca878`. Strict lifecycle receipt decoding now runs inside SqlPersistT under the current-session fence. It binds event, command UUID, target state and exact next version; malformed or foreign results throw a private typed exception before commit. The public invalid_database_response HTTP500 envelope is retained. The actual compiled/authenticated HTTP harness passes110 examples: eight injected corrupt results after real SQL writes leave lifecycle state, transition, audit and receipt rows unchanged; restoring the function permits one successful command and exact replay. Pure cases also cover malformed/cardinality/bound rejection envelopes and version overflow. Current-head hosted CI and fresh independent approval remain required.
